Title: THE ENIGMATIC SMILE
CustomInstruction: Four words or fewer. The whole painting turns on one ambiguous expression — name what she is doing, not who she is.

Title: A SWIRLING NIGHT SKY
CustomInstruction: Title the sky, not the village. Aim for something a museum label could carry: two to five words, no adjective you would not print.

Title: THE TOWERING SEA
CustomInstruction: There are three boats in this picture, and a mountain. Write a title that admits at least one of them exists.

Title: A GLANCE OVER THE SHOULDER
CustomInstruction: Good titles often name the one detail that will not let you go. Pick that single detail and build a title of five words or fewer around it.

Title: ARRIVAL ON THE SHORE
CustomInstruction: Name the event, not the figure. Aim for something that would work as a chapter heading.

Title: A CRY ON THE BRIDGE
CustomInstruction: One word if you can manage it, three at most. Say it out loud before you submit — this is a painting about sound.

Title: AN EMBRACE IN GOLD
CustomInstruction: Title it without using the words gold or love. That constraint forces you to look at what the two figures are actually doing.

Title: ABOVE THE CLOUDS
CustomInstruction: The man has his back to us on purpose. Write a title that keeps him anonymous and puts the landscape first.

Title: THE COMPANY STEPS OUT
CustomInstruction: This is a group portrait pretending to be an action scene. Title the action in five words or fewer.

Title: AN AFTERNOON IN THE PARK
CustomInstruction: Caption it like a photograph: name the day and the place. Specific beats poetic here.
